newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm further as Yeltsin op ends.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm further as Yeltsin op ends.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds edged up on Tuesday on news President Boris Yeltsin feels all right after a successful operation but dealers said an upward trend had set in in the morning anyway, despite Monday's news that more bonds had been frozen.
"We are seeing a slow rise now as the market has reacted to Yeltsin's successfull operation," Avtobank dealer Alla Zakharova said.

Moscow Business World bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said: "The rise started in the morning on the news the operation began. It would have been worse if it had been delayed or cancelled. The rise is noteworthy as trading is still thin."

A detective from the Moscow's district prosecutor office told Reuters on Monday it had issued an order to freeze $56.81 million in face value of bonds in June, bringing the total bonds currently known to have been frozen to $74 million.

The market has been less liquid since last Monday when the first rumours about further freezings started to circulate.. Dealers said trading is still thin and is conducted mainly through brokers to decrease counterparty risk.
Kovzharov added the current rise of Russian Vnesh debt was also helping MinFins.
Dealers said Minfins had firmed up to two big figures in early trading and a further 0.35-0.50 point after the surgery ended.
They added prices had stabilised at higher levels but could rise further when U.S. operators step in.
